thread_pair_example: kernel instance scan_nonfinal_kernel<..., DIMX=256> as launched by the driver (grid (2,1), block (256,1), DIMY=1), any block, any loop iteration k: thread 0 (warp 0) reads s_ftmp[0] at L145 (the 'Identify segment boundary' block) while thread 255 (warp 7) writes s_ftmp[0] at L157 two statements later; no __syncthreads between L140 (last barrier of the scan loop) and L160 (end-of-iteration barrier). The pair exists in every iteration of the lim=17 loop of both blocks. Write-after-read: if warp 7 reaches L157 before warp 0 executes L145, thread 0 sees the new flag instead of the previous iteration's one.
class_reason: Both accesses are plain: s_ftmp is a plain __shared__ char array, the read is an ordinary LDS.U8 and the write an ordinary STS.U8 (no volatile, no atomic, no .STRONG token in the SASS, no WARPSYNC emitted). The two threads are in different warps (0 and 7) of one block and no barrier or other synchronization orders them, so the pair is a data race (DR), not a strong-conflict (SC) pair.
buggy_expected: The pair (L145 read by thread 0 vs L157 write by thread 255, cross-warp WAR on s_ftmp[0]) is reported as DR in scan_nonfinal_kernel; the same detector must find the analogous pair in scan_dim_nonfinal_kernel (extra_pairs).

fixed.reason: The fix commit adds one __syncthreads() right after the 'Identify segment boundary' block (fixed file: L153 in scan_first_by_key_impl.hpp, L172 in scan_dim_by_key_impl.hpp). It is at loop-body level and reached by every thread that remains in the block (the 'retire warps early' return at the top only removes whole rows that are outside the array; with the driver's dims (8193,1,1,1) blocks_y = 1 and every thread stays), so the read at L145 is ordered before the write, which moves to L158 in the fixed file (s_ftmp[tidy] = flag; SASS @!P2 STS.U8 [R18+0xa08], R21 at 0x11f0, after BAR.SYNC at 0x1170). Nothing is expected for that pair in the fixed build (verify.expected_report_fixed).

Only s_ftmp races: s_tmp[tidy] (written at L156/L175) is read only at the top of the next iteration (L119 / L138, tidx==0 / tidy==0) after the end-of-iteration barrier (L160/L161 / L182), so by the source there is no s_tmp hazard even though the record text says 'and s_tmp'. boundaryid[] is written by at most one thread per row and iteration (the thread where the prefix-OR of the flags first becomes 1) and read after the loop barrier, so it has no hazard either.

open_questions: The record's expected_report_buggy says 'cross-warp shared WAR on s_ftmp (and s_tmp)'. By the source and SASS only s_ftmp has a concurrent reader (see sass_notes); the s_tmp write at L156/L175 is ordered against its reader by the barrier at the end of the iteration. If a detector reports s_tmp too, that would need a second look.

Natively the race window is very small (warp 7 must reach L157 before warp 0 executes L145 right after the same barrier); the smoke run on sm_75 shows no wrong result in either variant. Detection is by the detector's analysis, not by a wrong output.
